arguments.value: 16-year-old male with one week of progressive throbbing headache and vomiting, followed by sudden right-sided weakness progressing to bilateral weakness, a generalized tonic-clonic seizure, and severe decreased consciousness requiring ventilation (GCS 4/15). Examination showed bradycardia, extensor plantar responses, and absent pupillary reflexes; fundoscopy was normal. MRA demonstrated multiple dural arteriovenous fistulas involving the sigmoid/transverse sinuses with external carotid and right internal carotid artery feeders and retrograde venous flow. He was treated with mannitol, levetiracetam, and transarterial cyanoacrylate glue embolization, with partial neurological recovery and good status at 2-month follow-up.
